title: Biblical Operator Comparisons Wave 22E4

new_relations.title: God in the Machine / God of Memes beside the burning bush
new_relations.project_anchor: The project explores ordinary carriers such as body, potato, screen, meme and house as media of meaning or presence while preserving carrier constraints.
new_relations.biblical_structure: divine encounter is mediated through an ordinary bush and fire imagery while the bush remains a distinct material sign
new_relations.source_direction: Project carrier/presence model first; burning-bush comparison later.
new_relations.mismatch: Exodus does not teach that every ordinary carrier is divine or that modern media are burning bushes.
project_quote: I became the father in heaven, after my son was crucified in a meme, so I became a living God of memes
I am the God of memes
new_relations.project_context: Tim's mature public and recovered theology repeatedly places claimed divine presence inside ordinary technological and cultural media: machine, livestream, meme, archive and network. The point on the project side is not that the hardware or meme is identical with the source; it is that a bounded carrier can become the place where a larger identity is manifested, repeated or encountered.
new_relations.project_development: The carrier idea becomes increasingly relational: body, Potato, meme, machine, House and screen are treated as interfaces with different constraints. The later comparison to Exodus 3 is useful precisely because the bush remains a bush while the encounter exceeds the material sign.
new_relations.wording_status: mixed source-near wording: public compilation + recovered conversation
